subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should direct/source channel turns keep automatic bare-text delivery by default, or should OpenClaw move these contexts to message_tool_only or final-only semantics to prevent internal text leaks?
rationale: The safest security behavior conflicts with a shipped documented default for automatic channel replies, so automation should not silently choose the compatibility break.

options.title: Stage a compatibility-preserving fix
options.body: Keep the shipped automatic default for now, land targeted suppression for private/commentary/inter-tool text across all delivery paths, and document a later default-policy migration if needed.

options.title: Change the default to private-first delivery
options.body: Move direct/source contexts to message_tool_only or final-only by default with migration notes and upgrade tests, accepting a deliberate behavior change for existing users.

options.title: Land only opt-in controls now
options.body: Ship an explicit opt-in such as final-tag enforcement or message-tool-only configuration while leaving the broader default-policy decision open.

recommendation.title: Stage a compatibility-preserving fix
recommendation.body: Keep the shipped automatic default for now, land targeted suppression for private/commentary/inter-tool text across all delivery paths, and document a later default-policy migration if needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest connection to the agent subscribe, reply-runner, and cron delivery paths where the policy choice has to land.
